intended_object: The permutation automorphism group PAut(C) of an additive code C ≤ A^ι: the subgroup of Sym(ι) of coordinate permutations σ such that applying σ to the coordinates of each codeword maps C onto itself, i.e. {x ∘ σ⁻¹ | x ∈ C} = C. Inferred from the docstring and the name.
explanation: The definition is faithful. `reindex C e` is the image of C under `x ↦ x ∘ e`, as the simp lemma for its underlying set states. So the carrier is {e | {x ∘ e.symm | x ∈ C} = C}. This is the set of coordinate permutations that preserve the code, with the action x ↦ x ∘ e⁻¹ given in the docstring. It uses set equality rather than inclusion. That is the standard condition, and for infinite ι it is the right one. The proofs that the set contains 1 and is closed under multiplication and inverses are correct, so this is a subgroup of `Equiv.Perm ι`. The generality is natural: any additive group alphabet A and any index type ι. Mathlib has no dedicated permutation-automorphism group for codes. Abstractly this is a stabilizer under the coordinate-permutation action on subgroups, but Mathlib does not provide that action on `AddSubgroup (ι → A)` as a ready-made declaration, so there is no direct counterpart.
